contentHtml:
Tamul Waterfall (Cascada de Tamul) is the tallest waterfall in San Luis Potosí, with a 105-meter drop that plunges straight into the Tampaón River, in the municipality of Aquismón, San Luis Potosí. Every year, thousands of travelers come to the Huasteca Potosina drawn by its turquoise water, but few know exactly how much it costs, when to go or how to prepare. Tamul Waterfall takes planning: the only way in is by boat along the river, and conditions change with the season.

Tamul Waterfall: quick facts

AdmissionAdmission is $220 MXN plus $300 MXN per person for the panga (boat). Cash only: there's no ATM at the boat landing.
HoursDaily from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Boatmen stop heading out at 2 p.m.
Getting there45 min by car from Ciudad Valles to Tanchachín; from there, by panga up the Tampaón River
Best timeJanuary to April, when the water runs clear; arrive at 8:00 a.m.
TourTamul Expedition: from $1,550 MXN per person, 12 to 13 h, with pickup from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles

In this Tamul guide you'll find up-to-date prices, opening hours, transportation options and the tips only people who work in the region know. July and August are the busiest months on the boat route to the waterfall. Planning ahead is the difference between a smooth visit and hours of waiting at the boat landing.

Tamul Waterfall: how to get there and what to expect on the trip

How do you get to Tamul Waterfall from Ciudad Valles?

Tamul Waterfall is about 45 minutes by car from Ciudad Valles to the Tanchachín boat landing. The route follows Federal Highway 70 toward Río Verde, then turns off onto State Highway 27 toward Tanchachín, all the way to the boat landing. Admission is $220 MXN plus $300 MXN per person for the panga (boat), and it's cash only.

The travelers we coordinate usually prefer the Tamul Expedition, a 12- to 13-hour trip with pickup from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles, breakfast, entrance fees, a certified guide, safety gear and insurance, for $1,550 MXN per person. Book the Tamul Expedition ahead of time, especially in high season.

The boat ride on the Tampaón River

The only way to reach Tamul Waterfall in the Huasteca is by boat along the Tampaón River, about 45 minutes each way. The site is open daily from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Ideally, arrive at 8:00 a.m. Boatmen stop heading out at 2 p.m., so arriving late means missing the ride. Activities and prices at Tamul Waterfall in 2026

What is it like when you reach the waterfall?

Groups describe the first sight of it as an instant visual punch: the contrast between the rock, the tropical vegetation and the 105 meters of free fall is hard to anticipate from photos. The ideal season to visit is January to April: in the dry season the water runs clear and turquoise (most of all from March to May), though with less flow. In the rainy season, from July to October, the waterfall runs at full force, but the water can carry sediment. Check the best-time-to-visit calendar before you confirm your booking.

How much does it cost to visit Tamul Waterfall?

Prices in 2026: admission is $220 MXN plus $300 MXN per person for the panga (boat), cash only. Rappelling at Tamul Waterfall, with gear and certified guides, costs $1,700 MXN per person. For packages that combine the waterfall with rafting, see the guide to rafting on the Tampaón River.

Tips before visiting Tamul Waterfall

  • Arrive before 8:00 a.m.: The pangas fill up fast in high season. Leaving early guarantees you the first ride, with better light and less waiting.
  • Wear clothes that can get wet: Spray from the waterfall reaches the boats. Check the packing checklist for the Potosí jungle before you pack.
  • Pick your season carefully: the ideal season is January to April. In the rainy season (July to October) there's more flow, but the water can run muddy instead of turquoise.
  • Sun protection and bug spray: The boat ride lasts 45 minutes in direct sun. Use water-resistant sunscreen and long-lasting insect repellent.

Frequently asked questions about Tamul Waterfall

How tall is Tamul Waterfall?

Tamul Waterfall has a 105-meter drop, which makes it the tallest waterfall in San Luis Potosí in terms of free fall into a navigable river. The water plunges straight into the Tampaón River, in the municipality of Aquismón, San Luis Potosí.

How much does it cost to visit Tamul Waterfall in 2026?

Admission is $220 MXN plus $300 MXN per person for the panga (boat). CASH ONLY: there's no ATM at the boat landing. The Tamul Expedition, with pickup from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles, breakfast, entrance fees and a guide, costs $1,550 MXN per person.

What's the best season to visit Tamul Waterfall in the Huasteca?

The ideal season is January to April, during the dry season, when the water runs clear and turquoise. In the rainy season (July to October) the waterfall carries more water, but the river can run muddy. The waterfall is open daily from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Boatmen stop heading out at 2 p.m.

Is the visit safe for families with kids?

Yes, the panga ride on the Tampaón River is suitable for families with kids. We recommend booking an organized tour that includes life jackets and a certified guide. Rappelling is an optional activity for adults. Also see the family route through the Huasteca Potosina for more options.

Where is Tamul Waterfall, and how do you get there?

It's in Aquismón, San Luis Potosí, at the end of the Tampaón Canyon. From Ciudad Valles it's about 45 min by road to Tanchachín, and from there you go upriver by panga to the falls. Boatmen stop heading out at 2 p.m.

How long does a visit to Tamul Waterfall take?

On your own, plan on about 5 hours between the boat landing, the river trip and the ride back. The Tamul Expedition lasts 12 to 13 hours because it adds the Cueva del Agua (Water Cave) cenote and the Sótano de las Huahuas at sunset.

Where do you swim on the Tamul trip?

On the Tamul Expedition, at the Cueva del Agua cenote: it's a stop on the same canoe trip, on the way back from the waterfall, and that's where you swim and jump in.

What should I bring to Tamul Waterfall?

Cash for admission and the panga (there's no ATM at the boat landing), water shoes and about 2 liters of water per person. On the Tamul Expedition, safety gear, entrance fees and breakfast are included.

Is there a tour to Tamul Waterfall from Xilitla?

Yes. The Tamul Expedition includes pickup from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles, breakfast, entrance fees, a certified guide and the canoe trip, and costs $1,550 MXN per person. Lunch isn't included.
